543:
Any person who wishes to organize, form, or conduct any of the gatherings or assemblies regulated by this article shall be required to register with the chief of police a least four days in advance of the event, on forms to be provided by the chief of police, to obtain a permit therefor. An application for a permit to conduct the acts set forth in this article shall be made to the chief of police in writing, shall be signed by the person responsible for the conduct of the event, and shall contain the following information:
(1) The date and time proposed for the event.
(2) The route, place, or other area of the proposed event.
(3) The number of vehicles and the approximate number of persons who would participate in the proposed event.
(4) The name and address of the person sponsoring or promoting the proposed event.
(5) The name and address of the person making the application for the permit, and proper identification of that person.
(6) The name and address of at least five principal parties who will also be responsible for, or who may participate in, the event, including proper identification of these parties.
(7) The name, address, telephone number, and authorization of the sponsoring organization and its leaders if the activity is designed to be held by, for, or on behalf of any person, group, or organization other than the applicant.
(8) A statement as to whether the parade, assembly, or other activity will occupy all or only a portion of the width of the streets, the location of such streets, and any assembly areas for the group.
(Ord. No. 2020-001, 11-10-2020)
544:
The safety of Mt. Zion citizens and the protection of private property will be the determining factor in all decisions by the city involving the issuance of permits as described in this article. The city does not assume responsibility for the safety of march organizers, participants' vehicles, or equipment when an assembly conflicts with the peace and good order of the city once a n event is underway. Event organizers, persons requesting the permit, principal parties, and individua ls identified by law enforcement as agitators or facilitators, as well as those individuals actually committing a criminal act, will be prosecuted to the fullest possible extent allowed by state law and city ordinances. Marches, parades, protests, pickets, groups, or assemblies that stage outside the corporate limits of the city in an attempt to avoid permitting requirements and attempt to proceed into the city shall be stopped at the city limits by the Mt. Zion Police Department and other assisting agencies. The city also reserves its right to recover both compensatory and punitive damages through civil litigation. The city serves notice that it will stand with any Mt. Zion citizen involved in civil litigation as a result of any permitted or unpermitted assembly to include law enforcement testimony, video recordings, photographs, or physical evidence. It is the expectation of the city that all assemblies and events discussed in this article will be peaceful and conform to the guidelines that have been set forth. To ensure this end, the following requirements may be imposed by the city as a requirement for the issuance of a permit:
(1) An event policy from an accredited insurance company in an amount to be determined by the city.
(2) Escrowed funds considered adequate by the city to cover the cost of law enforcement personnel, expenses involved in trash cleanup, expenses associated with mutual aid agreements with county, state, or other municipalities, etc. Escrowed funds amount will be determined by the chief of police and in the possession of the city prior to permitting. A minimum amount of $100,000.00 is mandatory and any unused portion, if any, will be returned to the permit holder 60 days after the event.
(3) Portable restroom facilities shall be supplied by the event organizer in a quantity and manner acceptable to the chief of the Mt. Zion Police Department.
(Ord. No. 2020-001, 11-10-2020)

551:
(a) The City of Mount Zion is authorized to operate a public water and garbage collection service and to fix the charges, rates, fares, fees, and assessments therefore.
(b) Upon the failure of any customer or other responsible party to pay any bill, assessment, fee, penalty, or charge for water and/or garbage services for any premises for which that party is responsible, the city is authorized, through its designated agents, servants, and/or employees to turn off and discontinue water and/or garbage service to the property location for such nonpayment. Failure to receive a bill does not relieve the customer of responsibility for all applicable charges for water and/or garbage service incurred or imposed pursuant to these policies. The city shall not be required to resume the supply of water and/or garbage service to the property until all past due charges, including any applicable late fees, fines, penalties, or other charges are fully paid.
(c) All City of Mount Zion water customers shall be required to execute a service contract and related documents in a form and time frame satisfactory to the city.
(d) Upon the failure of any property owner to pay any bill, assessment, fee, penalty, or charge incurred by the property owner, the city shall have the right to impose a lien on the property on or for which water or garbage services are provided in lieu of or in addition to other remedies available to the city.
(e) The city shall be entitled to impose, transfer, or consolidate any outstanding balance due on one account to any other account in the name of or owned by the same person, entity, corporation, principal, or any legal successor thereto.
(f) The city requests that the customer be present at the location when service is turned on to prevent the possibility of any internal/external damage. The customer assumes all responsibility for water damage, if any, when service commences.
